teaser.text: Ford Motor Company sells Ford and Lincoln vehicles, then earns more from financing, parts, repairs, and services built around those vehicles. To follow a dollar through the business, start with what Ford sells, then trace who pays, what Ford spends, and how Ford Pro tries to make the relationship last.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Ford?

paragraphs.text: In the second half of 2026, Ford must deliver the cash recovery in its guidance while absorbing supply, tariff and warranty costs. Production-qualified prototypes for Ford’s Universal EV Platform—its planned vehicle architecture for a new generation of electric vehicles—are scheduled for the first quarter of 2027. Customer vehicles are due later that year. Ford Pro margins, Model e economics and warranty costs will show whether its established businesses can sustain the transition through 2029.

The base profit row moves from $10.2 billion in October 2027 to $10.5 billion in October 2028. It reaches $10.8 billion in October 2029. The starting point reflects the midpoint of Ford’s $10–11 billion 2026 EBIT guidance and the $10.208 billion average adjusted EBIT recorded from 2021 through 2024. Blue and Pro strength is expected to offset Model e losses. The bear row falls to $7.2 billion initially because supply, tariffs or warranty costs could overwhelm the recovery, then reaches $8.5 billion. The bull row rises from $11.5 billion to $14.5 billion if Novelis recovers, Blue and Pro exceed targets, and the Universal EV Platform launches on schedule.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Ford really make?

paragraphs.text: A strict measure starts with automotive cash from operations, subtracts capital spending, and subtracts stock-based compensation. Stock pay is not a cash payment to employees at that moment, but it is a real cost to shareholders because it dilutes their claim. Factories, tooling, software, pensions, and restructuring also compete for cash.

Ford’s preferred measure answers a narrower question. It excludes Ford Credit’s lending flows and certain cash uses, then adds selected distributions and other items. That can show the industrial business clearly, but the excluded bills still exist. The two measures pointed in opposite directions in 2025.

blocks.heading: How much does Ford pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend remains $0.60 per share annually because Ford declared a regular quarterly dividend of $0.15 and paid regular dividends of $0.60 in both 2024 and 2025. The bear case gives $0.40 after a cut to $0.10 quarterly. The bull case gives $0.80 by adding a $0.20 supplement, which is possible after cash recovery but is not guidance.

blocks.heading: Is Ford's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Ford paid out 95.5% of free cash flow in 2023 and 109.6% in 2024. In 2025, free cash flow was negative, yet dividends continued. Ford also spent $8.7 billion on capital projects in 2025 and planned higher spending for 2026. Its buybacks were designed partly to offset dilution from employee compensation and convertible notes, rather than simply reduce every investor’s ownership.

blocks.heading: What is Ford's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: The tables show revenue kept growing through 2025, but operating margin turned negative as EV reset charges hit. The memo’s real free cash flow and real free cash flow per share turned negative in 2025, while industrial net cash fell across the five years shown. The 6.5x forward P/E assumes forecast earnings become cash; the 4.8% dividend yield has no buyback yield, as 2025 buybacks were zero while stock pay continued.

blocks.heading: What do Ford's last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue fell from the prior-year quarter while operating income improved. Net income worsened because the BlueOval SK disposition charge reached US$3.612 billion. Adjusted EBIT rose to US$2.5 billion, and Ford raised its 2026 guidance. The quarter therefore looked stronger beneath the reported net-loss line.
Quarterly free cash flow remained uneven, reflecting investment and timing as well as profit.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in Ford's next results?

paragraphs.text: The decisive milestones are the second-half cash recovery, the handling of warranty and legal costs, and production-qualified Fathom prototypes in the first quarter of 2027. Together they will show whether Ford’s next stage becomes self-funded or makes a larger claim on its balance sheet.
